title: Mechanical properties of Cold Spray deposited NARloy-Z copper alloy
InformationInFigures: Yes. Particle size distribution (Fig. 1), YS (Fig. 5), UTS (Fig. 6), EL (Fig. 8), hardness (Fig. 9)

preSprayedProperties.Majority_Powder_Chemical_Composition: Bal. Cu, 2.6 wt% Ag, 0.4 wt% Zr

experimentalProperties.Deposition_Area_Dimensions: 150 mm long cylinder, diameter of 47.5 mm
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: Deposits were obtained in a vacuum tight chamber to avoid oxygen contamination. First the vacuum is performed and then the chamber is filled with helium gas. A closed loop system avoiding costly helium losses was also used. It consists in a system designed for cooling, filtering and compressing the gas in a closed loop circuit. In the present case, the spray process was performed at a chamber pressure of 480 mbar with less than 100 ppm of oxygen in the helium atmosphere. deposition started at room temp. but due to impinging particles the substrate temp. increased, but never exceeded 250°C. NOL ring tensile samples were made. Etching (using a 93.2% C2H3OH, 1.95% HCl, 4.85% FeCl3 solution) was performed before samples observation.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Few isolated pores with a diameter between 2 and 5 μm can be observed. distribution of additional elements, especially Ag, is not homogeneous

Experiments.Notes: CS1 As-Spray. The actual composition of the powder is given after analysis, so I used that instead of the given. deposition efficiency given as ratio between sprayed powder mass and deposit mass. It is made unclear in the figures the difference between CS1 and CS2, since they are grouped together as ~16 bar nozzle pressure, and near the end of the paper it combines these two as CS1/CS2. They have slightly varied other parameters so I will keep them separate for as-spray, but combine them for heat treated samples (using CS1 parameters) extracted from the figures since there is no indication of whether it was CS1 or CS2. Very rarely there were multiple samples for a given temperature anyway.
